# Load sample data

Load all records on "Open flowers" and "Leaves" for maple (_Acer_ spp.) in 2025.

```{r}
df_flower <- read_csv("alldata/input/NPN/flower/Acer/2025.csv") |>
  filter(phenophase_description == "Open flowers")

df_leaf <- read_csv("alldata/input/NPN/leaf/Acer/2025.csv")
```

# Clean data

We coded four ways to clean NPN status intensity data.

- Clean by resolving conflict: a function that groups by observer person ID and year, counts the total observations by an observer in that year. If there are conflicting observations for a phenophase of an individual on the same date, the observation from the observer with a higher total number of observations for that year will be kept. 

- Clean by leading no: a function that reviews observations for an individual, orders them chronologically, and counts the number of days since a "no" was last recorded. The number of days since previous no can be specified using the argument leading_window_days. Observations without a "no" observation within the designated leading window are removed. 

- Clean by trailing yes: a function that reviews data for an individual, orders them chronologically, and counts the number of consecutive "yes" observations. The number of days for a trailing "yes" can be specified using the argument leading_window_days. Observations without a "yes" observation in the trailing window are removed.

- Clean by window: a function that removes any observations within a defined set of dates. The window can be specified using the min_doy and max_doy arguments.  

We coded one function that combines all four ways together. 

- Clean data: a wrapper function that executes any of the four steps.

Load functions we developed for cleaning NPN status intensity data.

```{r}
source(here::here("code", "clean_data.R"))
source(here::here("code", "clean_by_resolving_conflict.R"))
source(here::here("code", "clean_by_leading_no.R"))
source(here::here("code", "clean_by_trailing_yes.R"))
source(here::here("code", "clean_by_window.R"))
```

Use these functions to clean flower and leaf data frames. We use all four data cleaning steps here.

```{r}
df_flower_clean <- df_flower |>
  clean_data(
    calculate_observation_option = "by_year",
    min_leading_no = 1,
    leading_window_days = 14,
    min_trailing_yes = 1,
    trailing_window_days = 14,
    max_doy = 213
  )

df_leaf_clean <- df_leaf |>
  clean_data(
    calculate_observation_option = "by_year",
    min_leading_no = 1,
    leading_window_days = 14,
    min_trailing_yes = 1,
    trailing_window_days = 14,
    max_doy = 213
  )
```

# Calculate and compare onset day

Load a function we developed for calculating the day of first yes.

```{r}
source(here::here("code", "calc_first_yes.R"))
```

Calculate flower onset date for both original and cleaned data frames.

```{r}
df_flower_onset <- df_flower |>
  calc_first_yes()

df_flower_onset_clean <- df_flower_clean |>
  calc_first_yes()
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
bind_rows(
  df_flower_onset |> mutate(group = "original"),
  df_flower_onset_clean |> mutate(group = "clean")
) |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, c("original", "clean"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group, y = day_of_first_yes)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.1) +
  labs(x = "Data cleaning method", y = "Day of year", title = "Flower onset") +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 10)))
```

Calculate leaf onset for both original and clean data frames.

```{r}
df_leaf_onset <- df_leaf |>
  calc_first_yes()

df_leaf_onset_clean <- df_leaf_clean |>
  calc_first_yes()
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
bind_rows(
  df_leaf_onset |> mutate(group = "original"),
  df_leaf_onset_clean |> mutate(group = "clean")
) |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, c("original", "clean"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group, y = day_of_first_yes)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.1) +
  labs(x = "Data type", y = "Day of year", title = "Leaf onset") +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 10)))
```

# Understand the effects of four data cleaning steps

Clean flower and leaf data using each data cleaning step, one at a time.

```{r}
df_flower_observation <- df_flower |>
  clean_data(
    calculate_observation_option = "by_year"
  )

df_flower_no <- df_flower |>
  clean_data(
    min_leading_no = 1,
    leading_window_days = 14
  )

df_flower_yes <- df_flower |>
  clean_data(
    min_trailing_yes = 1,
    trailing_window_days = 14
  )

df_flower_window <- df_flower |>
  clean_data(
    max_doy = 213
  )

df_leaf_observation <- df_leaf |>
  clean_data(
    calculate_observation_option = "by_year"
  )

df_leaf_no <- df_leaf |>
  clean_data(
    min_leading_no = 1,
    leading_window_days = 14
  )

df_leaf_yes <- df_leaf |>
  clean_data(
    min_trailing_yes = 1,
    trailing_window_days = 14
  )

df_leaf_window <- df_leaf |>
  clean_data(
    max_doy = 213
  )
```

Calculate the flower and leaf onset data for each of the applied cleaning functions.

```{r}
# Put inputs in a named list
ls_df_flower <- list(
  original = df_flower,
  `all methods` = df_flower_clean,
  `conflict resolution` = df_flower_observation,
  `leading no` = df_flower_no,
  `trailing yes` = df_flower_yes,
  window = df_flower_window
)

# Process all at once and bind into one data frame
df_flower_onset_all <- map_dfr(ls_df_flower, calc_first_yes, .id = "group") |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, c("original", "leading no", "trailing yes", "conflict resolution", "window", "all methods")))
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

# Visualize distribution of onset date
okabe_ito <- c(
  "#E69F00", "#F0E442", "#D55E00",
  "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#0072B2"
)

flower_master_onset <- df_flower_onset_all |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group, y = day_of_first_yes, fill = group)) +
  geom_violin() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = okabe_ito) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = .1) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("original", "leading no", "trailing yes", "conflict resolution", "window", "all methods")) +
  labs(x = "Data cleaning method", y = "Day of year", title = "Flower onset") +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10)), axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 10)))
```

```{r}
# Put inputs in a named list
ls_df_leaf <- list(
  original = df_leaf,

# Process all at once and bind into one data frame
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
```

# Calculate flower-leaf sequence (FLS)

We calculate FLS by subtracting flower onset date from leaf onset date. Negative values would indicate leaves emerged first.
```{r}
fls_raw <- inner_join(
  df_flower_onset |>
    select(site_id, site_name, latitude, longitude, individual_id, year, flower = day_of_first_yes),
  df_leaf_onset |>
    select(site_id, site_name, latitude, longitude, individual_id, year, leaf = day_of_first_yes)
) |>
  mutate(FLS = leaf - flower)

fls_clean <- inner_join(
  df_flower_onset_clean |>
    select(site_id, site_name, latitude, longitude, individual_id, year, flower = day_of_first_yes),
  df_leaf_onset_clean |>
    select(site_id, site_name, latitude, longitude, individual_id, year, leaf = day_of_first_yes)
) |>
  mutate(FLS = leaf - flower)
```

Visualize FLS before and after cleaning on maps.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4
#| echo: false

# load US map
us_map <- map_data("state")

# Visualize
sign_sqrt_trans <- function() {
  scales::trans_new(
    name = "sign_sqrt",
    transform = function(x) sign(x) * sqrt(abs(x)),
    inverse = function(x) sign(x) * (x^2)
  )
}

p_fls_raw <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(
    data = us_map,
    aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
    fill = "lightgrey", color = "white", linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = fls_raw, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, fill = FLS),
    shape = 21, size = 4, alpha = 0.5, stroke = 0.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#FFB81C",
    mid = "white",
    high = "#003594",
    midpoint = 0,
    transform = sign_sqrt_trans(),
    limits = c(-max(fls_raw$FLS), max(fls_raw$FLS))
  ) +
  coord_fixed(1.3,
    xlim = c(-125, -65),
    ylim = c(24, 50)
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(title = "Flower-leaf sequence (before cleaning)", fill = "Number of days")

p_fls_clean <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(
    data = us_map,
    aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
    fill = "lightgrey", color = "white", linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = fls_clean, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, fill = FLS),
    shape = 21, size = 4, alpha = 0.5, stroke = 0.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#FFB81C",
    mid = "white",
    high = "#003594",
    midpoint = 0,
    transform = sign_sqrt_trans(),
    limits = c(-max(fls_clean$FLS), max(fls_clean$FLS))
  ) +
  coord_fixed(1.3,
    xlim = c(-125, -65),
    ylim = c(24, 50)
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(title = "Flower-leaf sequence (after cleaning)", fill = "Number of days")

# join figures
p_fls_raw + p_fls_clean
```

# Infer latitudinal gradient of FLS

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4
#| echo: false

p_regression_raw <- fls_raw |>
  ggplot(aes(x = latitude, y = FLS)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(x = "Latitude", y = "Flower-leaf sequence (number of days)", title = "Latitudinal gradient in FLS (before cleaning)") +
  ggpubr::stat_regline_equation(label.x = 40, label.y = -250) +
  ggpubr::stat_cor(
    label.x = 40, label.y = -280,
    p.accuracy = 0.0001, r.accuracy = 0.01
  )
# p_regression_raw

p_regression_clean <- fls_clean |>
  ggplot(aes(x = latitude, y = FLS)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  xlim(30, 50) +
  labs(x = "Latitude", y = "Flower-leaf sequence (number of days)", title = "Latitudinal gradient in FLS (after cleaning)") +
  ggpubr::stat_regline_equation(label.x = 40, label.y = -60) +
  ggpubr::stat_cor(
    label.x = 40, label.y = -70,
    p.accuracy = 0.0001, r.accuracy = 0.01
  )
# p_regression_clean

# join figures
p_regression_raw + p_regression_clean
```
